title: QUIC internal server 0-RTT opening architecture
purpose: Define the narrow internal server 0-RTT path that composes early_data ticket advertisement, validated same-listener PSK resumption, REQ-QUIC-CRT-0152 admission, server ZeroRtt packet opening, and bounded application delivery without changing public support claims.
design_summary: Server early data remains internal and opt-in. A managed server advertises TLS early_data only when resumption tickets are enabled and a remembered 0-RTT transport-parameter snapshot exists. A client with a detached ticket that contains early-data prerequisite material emits zero-length ClientHello early_data before pre_shared_key and derives client 0-RTT packet-protection material from the resumption PSK and ClientHello transcript. The server accepts early data only after the resumption PSK binder validates and the listener-local anti-replay admission gate consumes the ticket. Acceptance publishes server ZeroRtt open material and zero-length EncryptedExtensions early_data. The runtime then opens Version 1 ZeroRtt long-header packets during the establishing server phase and delivers only the bounded STREAM/PING/PADDING subset into the existing application-data packet-number space and stream registry, while forbidden early-data frames produce protocol errors. Public APIs, IsSupported, HTTP/3, interop inventory classification, external persistence, and cluster-wide anti-replay stay outside the slice.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Server early data requires the existing internal managed resumption-ticket path and cannot be enabled by public API callers.
NewSessionTicket early_data uses the QUIC sentinel max_early_data_size value 0xffffffff.
ClientHello early_data is accepted only as a zero-length extension and pre_shared_key remains the last ClientHello extension.
The server consumes listener-local anti-replay state only after PSK binder validation and remembered transport-parameter acceptance.
Replay, disabled server early data, missing remembered parameters, or rejected parameters do not publish server ZeroRtt open material.
0-RTT runtime delivery is bounded to STREAM/PING/PADDING; forbidden ACK, CRYPTO, NEW_TOKEN, and HANDSHAKE_DONE frames are rejected.
The interop zerortt cell remains blocked until a live runner proof exists.
alternatives_considered: Promote zerortt interop support after internal runtime delivery proof. Rejected because the external runner cell still needs live proof and harness classification.
Expose public early-data options. Rejected because the support boundary is not ready for public API commitments or platform support claims.
Route 0-RTT through the full 1-RTT application packet handler. Rejected to avoid coupling early-data receive with 1-RTT key update, spin-bit, and retained-key lifecycle logic.
Advertise arbitrary max_early_data_size values. Rejected because QUIC uses the TLS early_data sentinel value rather than byte-granular limits.
risks: Expanding the frame set beyond the tested subset could accidentally admit state-changing early data before the trace and proof plan cover it.
Treating listener-local one-time consumption as cluster-wide anti-replay would overstate the design.
Changing public support classification before live zerortt proof would make the inventory misleading.
